conviction_note: Equifax's July guide was built on a 6.6% 30-year mortgage rate. The rate is now about 7.4-7.5%: the Fed has hiked, the 10-year is at 5.2-5.3% and MBA applications are at a 20-month low. Over the last month the sell-side cut its full-year EPS estimate by only 0.6%. So a Q4/full-year guide below consensus is the most likely surprise, and this name has sold off on weak guides before (-3.9%, -8.2%, -8.4%). Against that, the stock is already about 32% below its 52-week high and has bounced 15% off its 30 September low. There is also a margin story management can tell: VantageScore is now open to all lenders, and management puts full conversion away from zero-margin FICO pass-through at $40-50m of margin. So p_up is 42, not lower. The findings sum to -2.6 and the scaled number is -1.1 on a 7.0% absolute move.
bar: Q3 adj EPS $2.20 (19 analysts, one cut and none raised in the last month, AAII 2026-10-19: https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/517828-what-you-need-to-know-about-equifax-incs-q3-earnings). This equals the company's guide midpoint of $2.15-2.25. Q3 revenue guide is $1.68-1.71B, with consensus about $1.70-1.71B (https://finviz.com/news/370323/equifax-shares-fall-after-weaker-outlook-overshadows-second-quarter-earnings-beat-efx). July-dated sources show $2.27 and tickerleague shows $2.23; I treat $2.27 as stale. FY26 guide: revenue $6.71-6.78B, adj EPS $8.39-8.69, which implies Q4 EPS of about $2.08-2.38. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on revenue.
positioning_check: Short interest was about 7.0M shares, 5.9% of float, 3.1 days to cover at the 2026-08-19 settlement (https://equibles.com/stocks/efx/short-interest?range=all). Benzinga showed 6.3% and declining around 2026-09-04. That is not a crowded short. The baseline's 25-delta skew is -1.48 vol points (calls slightly richer), so the market is balanced to mildly upside. Put/call OI is 1.95 on thin total OI of 2,169. Event-implied move is 7.35%. Spot is $158.52: +7.6% over 5 days, +15.5% off the $137.24 close of 2026-09-30 (price on directors' Form 4s), and -32% from the 52-week high.

findings.finding: Management said on the Q2 call (2026-07-21) that its guidance 'embedded current mortgage rates', about 6.6% on the 30-year. Since then the Fed has raised rates 25bp, the 10-year is above 5%, Freddie Mac PMMS reads 7.40% (week of 2026-10-15) and MBA applications have fallen six weeks in a row to a 20-month low (week ending 2026-10-09). So the implied Q4 (EPS about $2.08-2.38) and the FY guide ($8.39-8.69) rest on a rate roughly 80bp too low. Meanwhile the FY consensus has fallen only 0.6% in the last month. A Q4 guide below the Street, or an FY cut toward the low end, is the likely release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2026-07-21 Q2 beat on EPS but the Q3 guide was below consensus, and the stock fell -3.93% on the window (-7 to -8.5% pre-market). 2025-07-22: -8.18%. 2025-02-06: -8.42%. All three were mortgage/macro guide disappointments. 2025-04-22: +13.84% when the guide held.
findings.why_not_priced: The rate move itself is public, but sell-side numbers have not followed. AAII shows the FY EPS estimate down only 0.6% in a month and 1.1% over three months, with one Q3 cut in the last month. If the Street had priced a guide reset, estimate revisions would be visibly negative and the stock would not have bounced 15% off its September low into the print.
findings.independence: Several sources agree. Rates: Freddie Mac PMMS 7.40% (https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms?intcmp=CWS). Applications: MBA via Trading Economics (https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/mortgage-applications/news/582398). Fed hike and 10-year >5%: HousingWire 2026-09-21 (https://www.housingwire.com/articles/lenders-brace-for-tougher-mortgage-market-forecast-reset/). Estimate drift: AAII 2026-10-19 (https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/517828-what-you-need-to-know-about-equifax-incs-q3-earnings). The company has not confirmed the transmission since July.

findings.finding: Q3 mortgage volume ran below the guide's assumption that originations would be down at 'the very low end of low single digits'. PennyMac's preliminary July-August funding was $16.6B against $34.9B for all of Q2, about -28% per month. Argus expects Q3 originations at least 5% below Q2. BTIG expects nonbank Q3 volume -3% against a +1% consensus. MBA refinance applications fell 9% in the week ending 2026-09-25, and Q3 2025 had a September refinance surge (refi index +42% YoY). On the other side, Equifax beat EPS in Q1 (+9.7%) and Q2 with the AI cost programme, so I net this to a small miss risk on Q3 revenue and an in-line EPS.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The reported quarter itself has not driven this name. EPS beats in Q1 2026 (+9.7%) and Q2 2026 were followed by -3.04% and -3.93%, both on the guide.
findings.why_not_priced: Q3 EPS consensus sits exactly at the guide midpoint ($2.20), which says the Street has not marked down Q3 mortgage. If it had, consensus would sit toward $2.15.
findings.independence: This is an industry proxy, not Equifax's own number. It shares a rate driver with finding 1 but uses Q3 data rather than the forward view. MBA weekly series: https://tradingeconomics.com/united-states/mortgage-applications/news/582398

findings.finding: On 2026-09-03/04 FHFA ordered Fannie and Freddie to approve all lenders for VantageScore 4.0, effective immediately. On 2026-09-29 VantageScore went onto the same GSE pricing grid as FICO Classic (FICO fell 27% that day). Equifax sells VS4 at $1 and earns no margin on the FICO scores it passes through, which are about 7% of revenue. Management put full conversion at '$40-50 million of incremental margin' (about 2% of EBITDA), and its July guide assumed 'limited VantageScore revenue'. The call is the first chance to quantify adoption and a 2027 margin tailwind, even as reported revenue falls from lost FICO pass-through.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior print has turned on VantageScore. The October 2025 FICO direct-license news hit bureau stocks 8-12% in a day, so this mortgage-score line moves the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The regulatory headlines were read as negative for the bureaus as a group, and EFX fell to $137 in September. The margin arithmetic (zero-margin FICO replaced by a $1 own-product score) needs the company to quantify it. If it were priced, the bureaus would not have traded down alongside FICO's 49% September fall.
findings.independence: The pricing-grid move and FICO's -27% are at https://www.asktraders.com/?p=255371 (2026-10-01). The $40-50m margin figure comes from the same Q2 transcript as finding 1 (https://www.webull.com/news/15265803862287360); that shares a document but not a fact.

findings.finding: Bloomberg reported on 2026-10-01 that FHFA plans to require only two of the three bureaus' reports (bi-merge) 'within weeks', possibly announced at MBA Annual on 10-12. EFX fell 5.9% after hours on that report. Pulte then cancelled his appearance and nothing has been announced. On the Q2 call management said '3B is here to stay', a stance it now has to defend or revise, and any share or price risk it quantifies lands on the 2027 mortgage line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bi-merge headlines: -5.9% after hours on 2026-10-01, and -5.9% after hours on 2026-09-03 (Pulte's post). Those were headline days, not prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced through the two -5.9% headline drops. What is not priced is management's quantification, which nobody has seen. The 7.25% group rally on 10-15 with no stated cause (TRU +10.7%, FICO +7.0%), which came after the Pulte cancellation (HousingWire 10-15), suggests some of the overhang was taken off before the print.
findings.independence: HousingWire 2026-10-15 on the cancelled appearance and the sidebar mention of a review of 'the use of multiple credit reports': https://www.housingwire.com/articles/pulte-mba-annual-reacts/

findings.finding: EFX goes into the print 15.5% above its 2026-09-30 close of $137.24 (directors' phantom-unit Form 4s). Much of that came on 2026-10-15, +7.25% to $161.26 in a bureau-wide move (TRU +10.7%, FICO +7.0%) for which no announcement was found. The rebound raises the bar the guide has to clear.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the 2026-07-21 guide-driven drop the stock rebounded +6.3% within a week (7-28). This name round-trips sentiment quickly.
findings.why_not_priced: The rebound is in the price by definition. The point is that the 5-day run-up of +7.6% removes the cushion a stock at its low would have. Short interest is 5.9% of float, so the move was not short covering into a crowded short.

findings.finding: Workforce Solutions' government vertical: the OBBBA Medicaid/SNAP work requirements start in 2027 and will require states to verify more often. About half of states use The Work Number, and management guided government 'growth in 2H'. The Q3 call is a natural place for an early 2027 framework that leans on it. A Senate Democratic investigation into Equifax's pricing (February 2026) is the counterweight.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print has turned on the government line alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely known. It is small because management has talked about it since 2025.
findings.independence: The guide comment is in the Q2 transcript: https://www.webull.com/news/15265803862287360

findings.finding: Hiring, which drives the talent-solutions half of Workforce Solutions' non-mortgage business, stayed flat. August JOLTS hires were 5.2M (rate 3.3%) and openings fell to 7.08M, a five-month low (BLS, 2026-09-29). September CPI came in hot at 3.7% (2026-10-14), so a further Fed hike is in play. Non-mortgage verticals are unlikely to offset mortgage in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Deutsche Bank cut its target after an earlier guide shortfall on lower mortgage and hiring volumes (undated).
findings.why_not_priced: Macro proxy, mostly priced. Filed small.

outside_window.finding: A formal FHFA bi-merge directive. Bloomberg says it takes effect 1-3 months after announcement, and no announcement has come. If it lands after 2026-10-21 it is a separate event.
OBBBA Medicaid/SNAP work-requirement verification volumes begin in 2027.

baseline_tension: The negative lean goes against a mildly call-rich skew (-1.48) but fits a 7.35% implied move that already expects a large reaction. A +7.6% run-up into a likely guide reset is the setup this name has sold before. Because the skew does not agree, p_up stays at 42, not lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (proxy smaller): the Q3 mortgage finding rests on PennyMac/Argus/BTIG/MBA proxies, not an Equifax number, and the name has a record of EPS beats, so I cut it from -0.5 to -0.3.
Rule 5 ('no cause' is not evidence): the run-up/positioning finding partly rested on the 10-15 rally having no explanation, so I cut it from -0.8 to -0.4.
Rule 5 (macro transmission): the hiring/CPI macro finding went from -0.3 to -0.2.

Rules 1 and 7: the guidance finding stays at -2.5 because this name has repeatedly sold on weak guides and the company itself tied the guide to the 6.6% rate. p_up moved from 40 to 42 for the mildly call-rich skew and the proxy weighting. abs_move stays at 7.0.
Pessimism-artefact note: the VantageScore margin positive and the government positive were left unchanged.
